guard: The runtime half of `two agents MUST NOT share a worktree concurrently` is real: the spawn-time guard refuses a live holder's tree as L4008, the refusal reads presence liveness so a dead holder releases with no bookkeeping, the holder registry is fed at spawn and reseeded at adoption, and the handle carries the logical worktree into the journal
proveWith: pnpm mutation-proof --config implementations/runtime/smoke/mutations/mesh-worktree.json   # --config resolves against the repo root, never the cwd
why: Lane F durable-actions step 8 (2026-09-03): the SPEC 6.5 worktree binding is a logical
contract with one rule, and the runtime enforces the half the validator cannot see. Each
obligation has a mutant: the guard call itself (W1), the presence-liveness read that makes a
dead holder's tree reusable rather than locked forever (W2), the registration that makes the
guard able to refuse at all (W3), the adoption reseed that keeps a resumed run enforcing what
its journal shows (W4), and the handle spread that carries the worktree into the journal and
the turn client's L4004 (W5). All five mutate mesh-handler.ts, which the suite imports through
a relative `../src` path — no build sits between the mutation and the run.

Batch B2 (2026-09-03) folds the adopted append log to the journal's keyed view before seeding: one record per step, so a turn is charged once, a failed spawn holds no worktree, and a cancelled turn is not re-registered.
